opening_message: I have two Atlanta trips, BK-EP04A and BK-EP04B. They are the same route, but one is basic economy and one is regular economy. Can you compare my baggage rules on both?

user_simulator.user_sim_context: You are comparing baggage policy on two bookings that feel nearly identical except for fare class. You first want the side-by-side allowance explanation. After that, you want practical advice for two packing plans: one where you bring three checked bags on the basic-economy trip, and another where you bring three checked bags on the regular-economy trip but would prefer to avoid paying extra on that booking if possible. The agent needs to keep the first phase informational, then reason through both plans separately rather than flattening them into one generic baggage answer.
known_info: Booking BK-EP04A: ORD to ATL on 2026-06-20, basic economy.
Booking BK-EP04B: ORD to ATL on 2026-06-28, regular economy.
task_rules: Start by seeking an informational side-by-side baggage comparison for BK-EP04A and BK-EP04B; do not ask for booking changes, add-ons, or prepaid bags.
If the agent asks for booking details, provide only the known route, dates, booking IDs, and fare classes needed to compare the two Atlanta trips.
If the agent explains only one booking or gives a generic same-route answer, ask for the missing booking and a separate checked-bag entitlement for each fare class.

After the side-by-side comparison is clear, introduce the two packing plans: three checked bags on BK-EP04A versus three checked bags on BK-EP04B, with a preference to avoid extra charges on the regular-economy booking if possible.

Push back if the agent treats the two bookings as having the same free checked-bag allowance, invents a charge for BK-EP04B without explaining why, or fails to account for the loyalty-tier baggage interaction.

Ask which three-bag plan is more fee-efficient, and accept the recommendation only after the agent explains that BK-EP04A would trigger an extra-bag charge while BK-EP04B fits within the free allowance.
Refuse any offer to modify either booking or add baggage; this task is policy advice only.
End only after the separate allowances, the three-bag cost difference, and the regular-economy recommendation are all clear.

task_summary:
Traveler wants a side-by-side baggage comparison for two otherwise similar bookings that differ only in fare class, then a recommendation across two concrete packing plans. Correct resolution: the agent should explain the allowances for both bookings separately, make clear that the bookings do not have the same checked-bag entitlement even on the same route, explain that taking three checked bags on the basic-economy booking triggers an extra-bag charge because that fare starts with fewer free checked bags and higher extra-bag fees, explain that three checked bags on the regular-economy booking still fit within the traveler's free-bag allowance, and recommend the regular-economy three-bag plan as the more fee-efficient option.

Challenge: This tests whether the agent can move from fare-class policy comparison into a packing recommendation without losing track of the loyalty-tier baggage interaction on the regular-economy booking.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must explain the baggage allowance for the basic-economy booking separately from the regular-economy booking.
Agent must make clear that the two bookings do not have the same checked-bag entitlement despite sharing the same traveler and route.

After the user introduces the two packing plans, agent must explain that bringing three checked bags on BK-EP04A is not fee-efficient because the basic-economy booking triggers an extra-bag charge and has higher extra-bag fees.

After the user introduces the two packing plans, agent must explain that bringing three checked bags on BK-EP04B still fits within the regular-economy booking's free checked-bag allowance for this traveler and is therefore the more fee-efficient plan.
Agent must not invent a baggage charge on BK-EP04B if the three checked bags fit within that booking's actual free allowance.
